description: Two pointed, long-toed shoes in dark green leather with gold stitching and curled gold tips, set on a grey stone floor. Each shoe has red and blue heraldic shield panels with gold fleurs-de-lis, lions and crowns, and one has a buckled strap. Dark blue hose show above, in an oil-painting style that fills the image edge to edge. There is no visible text, and a small white sparkle logo sits in the bottom-right corner.
reason: Shows a pair of late-medieval poulaine shoes with heraldic shields, but the card is the Mehen snake board game of ancient Egypt (about 3000 BCE). The footwear and heraldry are a clear anachronism for that year and do not show the game, its spiral snake board, marble pieces or lions.
